key_insight: IFCLoRA allocates LoRA rank before fine-tuning by using a topology-aware information-flow score, so each Transformer module gets adaptation capacity based on global task structure rather than only local gradients.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical way to improve parameter-efficient fine-tuning under a fixed compute and memory budget, especially when rank must be spent selectively across large models.
method: Build a sparse task-conditioned interaction graph from a small calibration set and a frozen pretrained model.
Combine global information-flow topology with local gradient sensitivity to compute Information-Flow Centrality for each LoRA-compatible module.
Assign the total rank budget once, producing a non-uniform rank profile before training starts.
evidence_signal: Across multiple models, tasks, and low-rank settings, IFCLoRA outperformed LoRA, AdaLoRA, and EVA under matched budgets; on LLaMA 3 8B mathematical reasoning it improved by 1.36 points at rank 4 and 1.82 points at rank 8.
watch_item: The method depends on a calibration set and graph construction quality, so rank allocation may be sensitive to how representative the pre-finetuning data and topology estimates are.
paper_title: IFCLoRA: Topology-Aware Rank Allocation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
